name: Patrode
subtitle: colocasia leaves layered with spiced gram flour, steamed into rolls and fried in slices

ingredients.note: catalogued as colocasia — you want the leaves, arbi patta, not the corm
keeps the paste from going rubbery
the acid that neutralises the itch in the leaves
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Choose young colocasia leaves. Old ones carry far more calcium oxalate and will leave your throat scratching however much tamarind you use.
Shave the thick central rib flat with a knife on the underside of each leaf, or the rolls will not lie flat.
Soak 30g tamarind in 150ml hot water for 20 minutes and strain to get the 3 tbsp of pulp. Do not skip it — it is doing chemistry, not just flavour.
The steamed rolls must cool completely, ideally 2 hours or overnight, before you slice them. Warm rolls crumble.

steps.text: Wipe the leaves clean and shave down the raised central ribs so each leaf lies flat.

Whisk the besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, jaggery, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, hing and salt with enough water to make a thick spreadable paste, about the consistency of peanut butter.
steps.tip: Too thin and it runs out of the rolls in the steamer. It should cling to a spoon turned sideways.

steps.text: Lay a leaf shiny side down, spread a thin even layer of paste over it, and lay a second leaf on top facing the opposite way. Build stacks of 4 leaves.
steps.tip: Thin layers. A thick smear steams into a wet, gummy centre.

steps.text: Fold the two long sides of each stack inward, spread a little more paste on the folds, then roll up tightly from the base into a firm log.
Steam the rolls seam side down for 25-30 minutes, until a knife pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Cool the rolls completely, at least 2 hours, then cut into 1.5cm thick slices.
steps.tip: Cold rolls cut cleanly. This is the difference between neat rounds and a broken mess.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, cut the heat for a minute, then pop the mustard seeds and sesame.
Lay the slices in a single layer and shallow fry 3 minutes a side until crisp and browned at the edges.
Drain, scatter with coriander leaves and serve hot with tea, or with rice and dal as part of a meal.

storage: The steamed rolls keep 4 days refrigerated unsliced and freeze for a month — slice and fry straight from cold. Fried slices are best eaten the same day.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
